title: Records and Structs
summary: Records for data with value equality, positional records, with-expressions for non-destructive changes, deconstruction, record structs; structs as small value types, copying semantics, readonly structs, and choosing between class, record and struct.

cards.q: What does with do on a record?
cards.a:
Creates a copy with the listed properties changed, leaving the original as it was

`p with { X = 5 }` copies every property of p and then changes X. The original record is untouched.

Assignments copy them, so code often changes a copy by mistake

A struct is a value type: assigning or returning it makes a copy, and the original stays the same. Changing every copy at once is what reference types do, which is why the bug is easy to miss.

cards.q: `record R(int A);` What is `new R(1) == new R(1)`?
cards.a:
True

Records compare by value: all properties are equal.
